title: Pin study jobs to the commit the study's pin.json names
summary: The core resolves a study job's source from athena.toml's repo_ref ("main"), ignoring the pin in studies/<id>/pin.json, so a re-study reads newer code under the old label. Change the pinning step in athena-core so that when the studied repository already has a study with a pin.json, the job pins that exact sha, and add tests. The audience is study producers and verifiers, who must see the mounted tree match the pin.

defaults_applied.how: Fix and tests are Rust in athena-core.
New tests plus cargo test, clippy, fmt criteria.
Fixes the pinning step that ignores pin.json, not the single study's citations.
Criteria assert which sha the pinner is asked for and the recorded pin.
Enforced in code with tests rather than a prose rule.
One focused change in pin_repo and its tests.
Behavior criteria name the cargo commands to run.
Doc comment and CHANGELOG explain the cause for outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Root cause, read from crates/athena-core/src/run.rs pin_repo and athena.toml [capabilities.study]: pin_repo uses only the global repo_url/repo_ref ("main") and never reads studies/*/pin.json, so any later study job gets the branch tip.

The request names no study, so the study is found from the repository: the sole study whose pin.json repository_url equals the configured repo_url, else the one whose study_id appears in the request text; otherwise the configured ref applies (a new study).
The fix is in the core pinning step, not in athena.toml: editing repo_ref to a sha would pin every future study to one commit.
The existing firstmate-work-handling study is not repinned or re-cited here; the user can ask for that separately.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test in crates/athena-core (run_pin_tests.rs) dispatches a study job whose head holds studies/<id>/pin.json with a repository_url matching the configured repo_url and a sha differing from what repo_ref ("main") resolves to. It asserts the pinner is asked for that sha, and the job record's pin sha equals it. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.

Tests cover the fallbacks: with no existing study for the repository the configured repo_ref is used as before; with several studies for one repository, the one whose id the request names is chosen, and if none is named the behavior is documented and never silently picks a different commit. Run: cargo test.

A pin.json whose sha is not a full 40-hex id, or whose pin does not resolve to that same sha, stops the job before dispatch with a message naming the study, rather than falling back to main. Run: cargo test.
cargo test --locked, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all --check all pass.

The doc comment on pin_repo and a CHANGELOG entry state the rule (an existing study's pin.json overrides repo_ref; athena.toml's repo_ref is used only for a new study) and name the cause: job 20261015-201650-cyvb mounted fc8972cd while the study pin said 6407052f.
No file under studies/, athena.toml or defaults.toml is changed; re-pinning or re-citing the study is a separate user decision.

out_of_scope: Re-pinning or re-citing studies/firstmate-work-handling to fc8972cd
Fixing the t3 local-only/scout wording in model.json and intro.json
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass odds than reference: the change touches core dispatch logic and needs new tests that read study files from the head commit, and the study-selection rule is a judgment call.
